Infrastructure Automation & CI/CD Documentation

Ansible | AWS | GitHub Actions | React

1. Project Overview

This project showcases a complete DevOps lifecycle: Provisioning an Ansible management layer on AWS to configure multiple environments (DEV, QA, PROD) and automating the deployment of a React/Vite application using a GitHub Actions self-hosted runner.

2. Ansible Architecture (AWS)

Infrastructure Details

  • Master Node: 1 EC2 Instance (Centralized Management).
  • Managed Nodes: 3 EC2 Instances (Categorized into DEV, QA, and PROD).

Implementation Steps

  • SSH Security: Configured secure access using PuTTY & Pageant. Enabled Agent Forwarding to ensure private keys remain secure on the local machine while allowing the Master node to connect to managed nodes.
  • Configuration Management: Wrote Ansible playbooks to automate the installation of Nginx across all nodes.
  • Status: Verified Nginx service via browser on all environment endpoints.

3. CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)

Automated the build and deployment process using a self-hosted runner sitting on an AWS EC2 instance.

Workflow Configuration (YAML)

name: Node.js CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: self-hosted

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup NodeJS
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Build Project
        run: npm run build

      - name: Success Message
        run: echo "sdhkxkx,xxvkvxkvj"

Deployment Highlights

  • React/Vite: Automated the optimized production build.
  • PM2 Integration: Integrated process management to keep the application running in the background.

4. Tech Stack Used

AWS EC2 Ansible GitHub Actions React/Vite Node.js Nginx PM2 SSH Agent Forwarding
